chunks: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur al-Ansari was in al-Medina while the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was in Mecca. Death came to him, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was in Mecca along with his companions, and the Muslims were praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

Al-Bara' bequeathed that when he was buried, his face should be directed toward the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) — toward the qibla. He also bequeathed a third of his wealth. Thus the Sunnah was established by this.

key_terms.السُّنَّة: Sunnah — prophetic practice or precedent that becomes binding or normative for the Muslim community
key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: The qibla — the direction of prayer, originally toward Jerusalem and later redirected to the Ka'ba in Mecca
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّة: Bequest, testamentary disposition — referring here to al-Bara''s disposition of a third of his estate
key_terms.ثُلُث الْمَال: One-third of property — the maximum a Muslim may freely bequest, a ruling later formalized in Islamic inheritance law

ai.seo_question: What is the story of al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur and the establishment of bequeathing one-third of wealth in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates the account of al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur al-Ansari, an early Muslim companion from Medina who, while dying during the early Meccan period before the change of qibla, made a testament directing his face toward both the Prophet and Jerusalem. This narrative is significant because it records how al-Bara''s intuitive choice to face the Prophet's direction — which coincided with the eventual qibla — and his bequest of one-third of his wealth became precedents that later became formalized as prophetic Sunnah. The hadith contextualizes Islamic inheritance law and burial practice within a formative historical moment.
word_analysis: came to him/presented itself to him

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan both together, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘Al-Bara’a Bin Marouf the Helper was at Al-Medina, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was at Makkah, and death presented itself to him, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was at Makkah, and his<sup>saww</sup> companions, and the Muslims were Praying towards Bayt Al-Maqdis,

and Al-Bara’a bequeathed that he should be buried and his face to be made to be facing towards the direction of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and bequeathed with a third of his wealth. Thus, the Sunnah flowed by it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ’Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur al-Ansariy lived in al-Madinah. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, lived in Makkah, and with his companions performed Salat (prayer) facing the direction of Bayt al-Maqdis.

Al-Bara’ made a will that said, ‘His face in grave must be kept toward the direction to which the Holy Prophet performs Salat (prayer) and about one-third of his legacy and thus the Sunnah was established.”’
